timeline.title: A Short History of Saying Yes
items: Romans marked a promise to marry with a ring, sometimes a simple band of iron.
Archduke Maximilian gave Mary of Burgundy a diamond ring, and a sparkly tradition began.
As queen, Victoria had to do the asking. She proposed to Prince Albert, and he happily said yes.
A copywriter dreamed up the famous line, and it became one of the best known slogans ever written.
today: The newest yes in the history of yeses. And our favourite by far.

facts.title: Fun Facts for the Newly Engaged
items: Rings go on the fourth finger because people once believed a vein ran from it straight to the heart.
Most diamonds formed deep underground well over a billion years ago. Talk about lasting.
Diamond is the hardest natural material on Earth. A very good sign for a promise.
Some penguins woo their partner with the perfect pebble for the nest. The original ring.
Albatrosses perform long courtship dances, and often stay with one partner for life.
Nerves and excitement feel almost the same in the body: racing heart, quick breath, shaky hands.
facts.hand: Science can explain the sparkle. It cannot explain how perfect {who} are together.

note.title: What we believe a yes is
note.contents: A note for the happy couple
paras: We make magazines for a living, and every so often one makes us grin from ear to ear. This was one of them.
We believe a yes is not one word on one special day. It is a promise to keep saying yes: to adventures, to hard days, to burnt dinners and to each other.
{who}, someone wanted to celebrate you properly. Not with a card anyone could buy, but with pages full of you: your story, your proposal, the nerves and the joy.
That someone is {from}. And from everything they told us, the whole world is cheering for you two.
note.wish: Congratulations, {who}. Here is to the next chapter.
